summary: The [Digital Transformation Blueprint 2025-2029](2025-05-01 A Blueprint for Mauritius - Digital Transformation 2025-2029) has an inter-ministerial committee behind it and no delivery report, milestone or revision published against it.
developments:
The blueprint was launched in May 2025 with new digital regulations announced alongside it, and an inter-ministerial coordinating committee was established in August 2025 ([blueprint](2025-05-01 A Blueprint for Mauritius - Digital Transformation 2025-2029), [committee](2025-09-01 Mauritius Establishes Inter-Ministerial Committee to Drive Digital Strategy)).

Fifteen months on, nothing has been published against it ([launch](2025-05-26-blueprint-digital-transformation-launch-lexpress), [regulations](2025-09-10 Mauritius Digital Transformation 2025-2029 - A Blueprint and New Digital Regulations)). Its interoperability commitments in particular have produced no instrument, and the framework they would replace dates from 2002.

summary: The [2025-2029 digital transformation blueprint](2025-05-27-blueprint-for-mauritius-digital-transformation-2025-2029) sits under a 2030 strategic plan, with a national data strategy added in 2026.
developments:
The long-horizon instrument is the 2030 strategic plan of December 2018 ([plan](2018-12-17-digital-mauritius-2030-strategic-plan)); the blueprint of May 2025 is the current term's programme under it ([blueprint](2025-05-27-blueprint-for-mauritius-digital-transformation-2025-2029)).

A national data strategy for 2025 to 2029 was published in January 2026, the first instrument to revisit the 2017 open data policy ([strategy](2026-01-28-mauritius-national-data-strategy)).

The base holds three live strategy instruments and no published measurement against any of them. The one progress account on file is the digital government transformation strategy's own update of April 2025 ([update](2025-04-25-digital-government-transformation-strategy-progress-update)).

summary: The [broadband policy ran to 2020](2012-01-20-national-broadband-policy-2012-2020) and has no successor; what moves instead is spectrum, by regulator decision.
developments:
The national broadband policy covers 2012 to 2020 and is the only broadband policy on file ([policy](2012-01-20-national-broadband-policy-2012-2020)).

Six years past its horizon, the instruments actually moving broadband are the regulator's: the 700 MHz band opened for IMT and 5G in December 2025 ([decision](2025-12-22-icta-700mhz-imt-5g-decision)) and the 2300-2400 MHz band in June 2026 ([decision](2026-06-04-icta-2300-2400mhz-imt-5g-decision)).

No replacement policy, coverage target or universal service obligation is held. The policy layer has fallen behind the licensing layer rather than directing it.

summary: No cloud or storage policy is held; a [sovereign cloud market sounding](2025-09-19-sovereign-cloud-rfi-clarification-no-2) reached its second clarification in September 2025.
developments:
A request for information for a sovereign cloud for government reached a second clarification in September 2025 ([clarification](2025-09-19-sovereign-cloud-rfi-clarification-no-2)).

A scale-out storage solution for the government online centre was tendered in October 2025 ([tender](2025-10-06-scale-out-storage-solution-goc-tender)) and awarded in March 2026 ([award](2026-03-27-goc-scale-out-storage-solution-award)).

The procurement is running ahead of the policy: no instrument states where government data must be held, what may be hosted abroad, or on what terms cloud services are bought.

summary: The [national data strategy](2026-01-28-mauritius-national-data-strategy) of January 2026 is the first roadmap over a sharing platform that has run since 2016.
developments:
The sharing layer is the older half: a platform in service since 2016 through which government agencies exchange data ([platform](2016-08-01-infohighway-data-sharing-platform)).

A national data strategy for 2025 to 2029 was published in January 2026 and names that platform as what it builds on ([strategy](2026-01-28-mauritius-national-data-strategy)).

Data measures were carried into the 2026-2027 budget in June ([budget](2026-06-19-budget-speech-2026-2027-startup-revolution)). What the base does not hold is a technical interoperability standard, a service catalogue, or a count of agencies connected to the platform.

summary: A [National AI Strategy and its FAIR guidelines](2026-04-12-national-ai-strategy-fair-guidelines-launch-lexpress) run on six pillars to 2029, with an artificial-intelligence unit from December 2025 and a [first innovation lab](2026-08-21-cajnews-mauritius-ai-innovation-lab-stempower) in August 2026.
developments:
The guidelines are vendor-neutral and border-agnostic, governing by impact rather than geography ([guidelines](2026-04-23-ai-strategy-fair-ethics-before-execution-techcabal), [launch](2026-04-12-national-ai-strategy-fair-guidelines-launch-lexpress)).

The strategy runs 2025-2029 with an artificial-intelligence unit established in December 2025, and a first innovation lab was inaugurated at the cybercity in August 2026 with a memorandum signed at the event; the lab's capacity, funding and access terms are not published ([lab](2026-08-21-cajnews-mauritius-ai-innovation-lab-stempower)).

summary: No localisation rule is held; the [2017 Data Protection Act](2017-12-22-data-protection-act-2017) governs transfers, and sovereign cloud is a procurement rather than a policy.
developments:
The Act of December 2017 is the governing instrument and regulates transfer abroad rather than requiring local storage ([Act](2017-12-22-data-protection-act-2017)).

A sovereign cloud for government is being market-sounded ([clarification](2025-09-19-sovereign-cloud-rfi-clarification-no-2)), and the 2026-2030 fintech strategy sets out where financial data is expected to sit ([strategy](2026-05-22-mauritius-national-fintech-strategy-2026-2030)).

Neither is an instrument requiring state or personal data to be held in country, and none is held. Sovereignty here is being bought as infrastructure before it is written as rule.

summary: A [National Data Strategy 2025-2029](2026-02-01-national-data-strategy-2025-2029-launch-lexpress) was launched in January 2026 and a separate [data governance strategy](2026-07-16-mauritius-america-india-connect-subsea-cable-allmyt-summit-mitci) was committed to in July, with no text published.
developments:
The data strategy was launched on data protection day around responsible data governance, cybercrime prevention and online protection of minors, with a memorandum signed between the police, the data-protection office and the national computer emergency team ([strategy](2026-02-01-national-data-strategy-2025-2029-launch-lexpress), [preparation](2025-04-09-ict-data-protection-strategy-in-preparation-lexpress)).

A national data governance strategy was separately committed to at an operator summit in July 2026, alongside forthcoming amendments to the data protection statute aimed at cybersecurity, privacy and online safety for children; no text, timetable or introduction date is published ([commitment](2026-07-16-mauritius-america-india-connect-subsea-cable-allmyt-summit-mitci)).

summary: The [national open data policy of May 2017](2017-05-01-national-open-data-policy) stands unamended; a statistics platform launched in 2025 is the practical movement.
developments:
The policy was published in May 2017 and is still the governing instrument ([policy](2017-05-01-national-open-data-policy)).

The statistics office launched a data platform with United Nations development agency support on World Statistics Day 2025 ([launch](2025-10-22-undp-statistics-mauritius-maustats-platform-launch)).

The 2026 national data strategy is the first instrument to revisit the policy's ground ([strategy](2026-01-28-mauritius-national-data-strategy)). No dataset count, licence statement or publication mandate under the 2017 policy is held.

progress: Mixed, officer regulations promulgated while the Act itself was left out of an omnibus amending fifty-eight statutes
summary: [Data Protection Officer Regulations](2026-06-12-dpo-regulations-2026-lexpress) were promulgated in June 2026 for January 2027, while the [Data Protection Act 2017](2026-07-24-mauritius-economic-financial-measures-misc-provisions-bill-xiii-2026) is not among the fifty-eight Acts the omnibus amends.
developments:
The regulations formalise designation, qualifications, independence and reporting duties for data protection officers across public and private sectors, with a six-month compliance window ([regulations](2026-06-12-dpo-regulations-2026-lexpress)).

Amendments to the Act itself were committed in July 2026 with no text, timetable or introduction date ([commitment](2026-07-16-mauritius-america-india-connect-subsea-cable-allmyt-summit-mitci)), and the Act is not among the fifty-eight statutes the omnibus bill amends ([bill](2026-07-24-mauritius-economic-financial-measures-misc-provisions-bill-xiii-2026)). The year's expanded inter-agency data sharing therefore arrives with no matching safeguards amendment ([assessment](2026-05-27-no-digital-id-without-data-protection-madhub-biometricupdate)).

summary: The [Cybersecurity and Cybercrime Act 2021](2021-11-24-mauritius-cybersecurity-cybercrime-act-2021) has been in force since December 2021 and carries the fake-profile, cyberbullying and undesirable-content offences.
developments:
The enacted text as gazetted is held, carrying the offences of misuse of a fake profile, cyberbullying and failure to moderate undesirable content with their penalty scales ([Act](2021-11-24-mauritius-cybersecurity-cybercrime-act-2021)).

It is the statute the ministry's own online-content warnings rest on, and no charge, prosecution or takedown count under any of those sections is published in this base.

summary: The [1985 identity card Act](1986-04-11-national-identity-card-act-version-3) carries the digital card through 2024 regulations, with the 2026 Finance Act amending around it.
developments:
The Act has been in force since April 1986 and is the statutory basis for the card ([Act](1986-04-11-national-identity-card-act-version-3)); the regulations of February 2024 set the terms on which the card and the mobile identity are issued and read ([regulations](2024-02-16-national-identity-card-regulations-2024)).

The Finance Act 2026, assented in August, carries the statutory changes behind the budget's identity and registry measures ([Act](2026-08-12-finance-act-2026)).

The Electronic Transactions (Amendment) Act 2026 was enacted in May ([Act](2026-05-25-electronic-transactions-amendment-act-2026)). A forty-year-old card statute is doing the work, extended by regulation rather than replaced.

summary: The [2018 payment systems Act](2018-11-29-national-payment-systems-act-2018) is the governing statute; a payment aggregator guideline was issued under it in July 2026.
developments:
The Act was assented in November 2018 and is now at its seventh consolidated version ([Act](2018-11-29-national-payment-systems-act-2018), [consolidation](2019-01-31-national-payment-systems-act-2018)).

The central bank issued a guideline for payment aggregators in July 2026, bringing them under a stated supervisory expectation for the first time ([guideline](2026-07-01-guideline-for-payment-aggregators)).

The financial-crime statute book was amended in April 2026 ([Act](2026-04-17-aml-cft-cpf-miscellaneous-provisions-act-2026)). No enforcement action, licence refusal or sanction under the payments Act is held.

summary: An [omnibus bill](2026-07-24-mauritius-economic-financial-measures-misc-provisions-bill-xiii-2026) of 119 pages amending fifty-eight Acts carries the fintech committee, the artificial-intelligence city scheme, a threat-sharing platform and a digital travel authorisation.
developments:
The bill was introduced on 24 July 2026 with staged commencement from 1 September and several provisions deemed retrospective ([bill](2026-07-24-mauritius-economic-financial-measures-misc-provisions-bill-xiii-2026)).

A secondary account put the figure at some sixty laws; the enacting text gives fifty-eight amended and one repealed ([account](2026-07-27-lexpress-finance-bill-etat-pilote-par-les-donnees)). It is the single largest legislative vehicle in the country's digital record, and it was introduced and not enacted.

summary: The [higher education AI regulations of April 2026](2026-04-03-higher-education-use-of-ai-regulations-2026) are the country's only binding artificial-intelligence instrument.
developments:
Government Notice 39 of 2026 makes regulations on the use of artificial intelligence in higher education ([regulations](2026-04-03-higher-education-use-of-ai-regulations-2026)).

The national strategy and its fairness, accountability, inclusiveness and responsibility guidelines are non-binding ([strategy](2026-02-13-mauritius-national-ai-strategy), [guidelines](2026-02-13-mauritius-fair-guidelines-ai)).

The higher education regulator issued amended guidelines of its own in May 2026 ([guidelines](2026-05-13-hec-ai-guidelines-higher-education-amended)). What the base does not hold is any general artificial-intelligence statute, bill or regulator: the one binding rule reaches universities only.

summary: A [virtual-asset solicitation rule](2026-07-24-mauritius-economic-financial-measures-misc-provisions-bill-xiii-2026) in the omnibus bill would presume any publicly accessible communication targets Mauritius, and [electronic transactions amendments](2026-07-30-lexpress-secteur-postal-cyberattaques-post-isac) were referred to in July 2026.
developments:
Unlicensed solicitation of investors would be prohibited by any medium, defined to reach targeted or algorithmic advertising, platforms, applications, social media, influencers, affiliates, referral codes, seminars and webinars, with any publicly accessible communication presumed to target the country; the presumption shifts the burden onto an offshore promoter to show it was not soliciting locally ([rule](2026-07-24-mauritius-economic-financial-measures-misc-provisions-bill-xiii-2026)).

Amendments modernising the digital-commerce framework and consumer protection were referred to by the minister at a postal-sector workshop, with no text, timetable or introduction date published ([amendments](2026-07-30-lexpress-secteur-postal-cyberattaques-post-isac)).

summary: The [Statistics Act 2000](2000-01-01-statistics-act-2000-consolidated) is under revision, with the office's independence carried in the 2026-2027 budget annex.
developments:
The Act has been in force since April 2001 and is held in its consolidated, amended form ([Act](2000-01-01-statistics-act-2000-consolidated)).

The 2026-2027 budget annex carries the independence of the statistics office ([annex](2026-06-19-budget-annex-2026-27-statistics-act-independence)), and the Finance Act 2026 amends the statute book around it ([Act](2026-08-12-finance-act-2026)).

An observance of standards and codes data module assessed the statistical system in December 2025 ([assessment](2025-12-10-imf-mauritius-rosc-data-module)). The independence provision is announced; no amending text is held.

summary: A [Freedom of Information Bill](2026-02-01-national-data-strategy-2025-2029-launch-lexpress) was announced as in preparation in February 2026, and no draft, text or timetable has been published since.
developments:
The bill was announced by the data-protection commissioner at the launch of the national data strategy ([announcement](2026-02-01-national-data-strategy-2025-2029-launch-lexpress)).

Six months on, nothing has followed. The country has a data-protection statute aligned to the European regulation and no statutory right of access to public information to sit beside it.

summary: The office runs about [3,000 enforcement actions a year](2026-05-27-no-digital-id-without-data-protection-madhub-biometricupdate) with 99 per cent resolved amicably, and is [pursuing a European adequacy assessment](2026-05-27-no-digital-id-without-data-protection-madhub-biometricupdate).
developments:
Enforcement volume was set out at an international identity meeting in May 2026: about 3,000 actions a year, 99 per cent resolved amicably, chief data officers mandated and administrative fines being added by amendment ([enforcement](2026-05-27-no-digital-id-without-data-protection-madhub-biometricupdate), [formula](2026-05-16 World Bank, African DPAs outline formula for trusted digital identity, DPI)).

Adequacy is being pursued with full alignment of the law to the European regulation, and no application date, assessment stage or decision is published ([adequacy](2026-05-27-no-digital-id-without-data-protection-madhub-biometricupdate)).

progress: Regressed, large-scale interception still running without judicial oversight while a new plate-recognition system was installed on public premises with no privacy assessment
summary: [Interception described in Parliament as running since 2017 without judicial oversight](2025-02-07-in-the-shadows-of-mass-surveillance-mauritiustimes) has no reform instrument, and an [airport plate-recognition system](2026-08-16-lexpress-mu-aeroport-ssr-systeme-stationnement-anpr) was installed with no retention rule published.
developments:
Large-scale interception was described in Parliament as running since 2017 without judicial oversight, wired into major operators and accessed by counter-terrorism and national security units; no reform instrument, inquiry outcome or judicial-authorisation requirement has been published, and leaked recordings continue to test the framework ([interception](2025-02-07-in-the-shadows-of-mass-surveillance-mauritiustimes), [leaks](2026-07-13-privacy-of-communications-moustass-leaks-mauritiustimes)).

An airport parking system with more than twenty licence-plate-recognition cameras entered full operation in August 2026 at a cost of Rs 50 million, replacing a 2013 installation; no retention period, data controller or privacy assessment is published ([system](2026-08-16-lexpress-mu-aeroport-ssr-systeme-stationnement-anpr)).

summary: The country ran two regional tracks in 2026: [Indian Ocean governance in April](2026-04-11-ioc-2026-collective-stewardship-indian-ocean-governance) and the southern African summit in August.
developments:
The government programme for 2025 to 2029 sets regional cooperation as a standing commitment ([programme](2025-01-24-government-programme-2025-2029)).

An Indian Ocean Commission meeting in April 2026 promoted regional cooperation and sustainable governance ([meeting](2026-04-11-ioc-2026-collective-stewardship-indian-ocean-governance)).

Cabinet noted the southern African bloc's 46th summit in August 2026 ([Cabinet](2026-08-14-cabinet-highlights-sadc-46th-summit)). Neither account names a digital instrument, a data-sharing arrangement or a harmonisation commitment among what was agreed.

summary: The regional justice ministers [called for signature and ratification](2026-06-05-sadc-justice-ministers-legal-instruments) of the bloc's legal instruments in June 2026; nothing was ratified.
developments:
The committee of ministers of justice and attorneys general called for enhanced cooperation and for signature, ratification, accession to and implementation of the bloc's legal instruments ([call](2026-06-05-sadc-justice-ministers-legal-instruments)).

Which instruments Mauritius has yet to ratify is not stated in the account, and no ratification is recorded against it.

What the country has ratified on the data side is the Council of Europe protocol, in September 2020, which is a different track from the regional one ([ratification](2020-09-04-mauritius-ratification-convention-108-plus)).

progress: Regressed, the continental internet registry seated here left with an unresolved authority chain and an undischarged receiver
summary: The [continental internet registry](2026-08-10-btw-media-afrinic-eight-seat-board-election-evidence-gap) named one person to all eight board seats while withholding the vote tallies its own guidelines promised, and the [appeal court set aside its appeal](2024-10-15-mauritius-afrinic-v-cloud-innovation-2024-scj-473-judgment) for want of corporate authority.
developments:
The appeal court had directed in October 2024 that the board be reconstituted within two months, describing it as a matter of utmost urgency, in substitution for the six months ordered in 2023 ([judgment](2024-10-15-mauritius-afrinic-v-cloud-innovation-2024-scj-473-judgment)).

The registry named a person to all eight seats in September 2025, some nine months past that deadline, while withholding every candidate vote tally its own election guidelines promised ([election](2026-08-10-btw-media-afrinic-eight-seat-board-election-evidence-gap)).

The appeal court then set aside the registry's 2023 appeal for lack of corporate authority without ruling on the official receiver's permission or on statutory leave, leaving the authority chain from election through appointment to quorum unresolved and the receiver undischarged ([appeal](2026-08-13-btw-media-afrinic-appeal-receiver-permission-statutory-leave)).

summary: Transfers run under the [2017 Act](2017-12-22-data-protection-act-2017) and the [Convention 108+ protocol](2020-09-04-mauritius-ratification-convention-108-plus) ratified in 2020; the European adequacy assessment is open.
developments:
The Act of 2017 governs transfer abroad ([Act](2017-12-22-data-protection-act-2017)), and the amending protocol to the Council of Europe data convention was ratified in September 2020, among the first ratifications outside Europe ([ratification](2020-09-04-mauritius-ratification-convention-108-plus)).

The national data strategy of January 2026 sets cross-border flows as a workstream ([strategy](2026-01-28-mauritius-national-data-strategy)).

Cabinet's February 2026 decisions record the social register being used for a connectivity measure rather than any transfer arrangement ([Cabinet](2026-02-06-cabinet-highlights-internet-gratis-srm)). No transfer authorisation, refusal or adequacy finding is held.

summary: The [e-Government Interoperability Framework](2002-11-01 Mauritius e-Government Interoperability Framework v1.0) dates from 2002 and no successor is held, twenty-four years on.
developments:
Cabinet noted a Digital Service Framework on 28 August 2026 setting mandatory principles and standards for every government digital service, from procurement through maintenance ([framework](2026-09-01-gis-mauritius-digital-service-framework)). It is noted, not yet issued, and no compliance date is stated.

Version 1.0 was published in November 2002 and remains the standing interoperability instrument ([framework](2002-11-01 Mauritius e-Government Interoperability Framework v1.0), [case study](2024-03-01 Enhancing Data-Sharing Practices Between Government Agencies (case study, Sone Osakwe))).

The interoperability commitments of the 2025-2029 blueprint have produced no published instrument. A country running a mobile identity wallet, an instant payment switch and a Tier IV sovereign facility is doing so on an interoperability framework older than any of them.

summary: The [standards bureau](2022-06-30-msb-annual-report-2021-2022) made two instruments inside two months in 2026 — a certification mark and appliance efficiency standards.
developments:
The bureau's last published annual report covers 2021 to 2022 ([report](2022-06-30-msb-annual-report-2021-2022)).

Certification mark regulations were made in April 2026 ([regulations](2026-04-09-msb-certification-mark-regulations-2026)), and minimum energy performance standards for refrigerating appliances in May ([regulations](2026-05-16-energy-efficiency-refrigerating-appliances-regulations-2026)).

No standard for digital services, procurement or accessibility is held, and no annual report later than 2021-2022 is on file, so the bureau's current throughput cannot be read.

summary: The postal operator is being wired into a [global postal information-sharing centre](2026-07-30-lexpress-secteur-postal-cyberattaques-post-isac) with an international security standard urged, and the state operator co-chairs [model-as-a-service certification work](2026-07-20-mauritius-telecom-tm-forum-modaas-telecomtv).
developments:
The national postal operator is being connected to the postal union's global information-sharing centre and the minister urged adoption of the international information-security management standard; no membership date or commitment is published ([postal](2026-07-30-lexpress-secteur-postal-cyberattaques-post-isac)).

Work to define controls and conformance criteria for a model-as-a-service certification framework began in July 2026, with the state operator a founding contributor and co-chair; the framework does not yet exist, and the standards body's own research finds 72 per cent of operator leaders say they trust their production artificial intelligence while 14 per cent can evidence it ([certification](2026-07-20-mauritius-telecom-tm-forum-modaas-telecomtv)).

summary: A [national internet governance forum](2026-08-11-mauritius-blockchain-for-good-bybit-igf) convened in 2026 with the Vice President and the minister attending, and the clearest [domestic objection to the AI-first framing](2026-08-02-lexpress-mauritius-needs-faster-justice-not-just-ai) was published in August.
developments:
The forum is a national multi-stakeholder body founded by a civil-society movement; at its 2026 meeting a visiting alliance and an exchange met the Vice President and the minister to discuss artificial intelligence, cybersecurity and digital-trust frameworks for small island states. The record held is the visiting alliance's own release, and no programme, outcome document or attendance figure is held ([forum](2026-08-11-mauritius-blockchain-for-good-bybit-igf)).

A named analyst argued in August 2026 that contract enforcement rather than technology is what limits the economy, prescribing digitalised case management alongside a small-claims process and a stronger commercial division rather than instead of them ([argument](2026-08-02-lexpress-mauritius-needs-faster-justice-not-just-ai)). It is analysis rather than evidence, and it is the only domestic objection on file to the framing the budget adopts.

progress: Regressed, the state restating criminal exposure for online speech and consulting on identity verification for social media
summary: A [ministerial communique](2026-08-17-lexpress-mu-reseaux-sociaux-sanctions-contenus) restated penalties of up to Rs 1m and twenty years for online content, and [identity verification for social media](2026-06-07-social-media-identity-verification-consultations-lexpress) went to consultation.
developments:
The communique restated that the 2021 Act penalises false profiles, cyber-harassment and the diffusion of undesirable content, that administrators of accounts, pages and groups must moderate flagged content when a competent authority reports it, and that penalties reach a fine of Rs 1m and up to twenty years' penal servitude ([communique](2026-08-17-lexpress-mu-reseaux-sociaux-sanctions-contenus)). It creates no new obligation and is enforcement signalling on a law five years old.

A parallel communique defined undesirable content to include material that is deceptive or inaccurate ([warning](2026-08-17-mitci-mauritius-communique-responsible-use-social-media)).

Consultations opened in June 2026 toward a social-media identity verification mechanism, citing 2,300 online-harm cases in six months and frauds up to Rs 500,000 ([consultation](2026-06-07-social-media-identity-verification-consultations-lexpress)); the minister acknowledged the privacy and free-expression tension and the need to negotiate with platforms ([consultation](2026-06-07-social-media-identity-verification-consultations-lexpress)).

summary: The [2026-2027 budget](2026-06-20-budget-2026-2027-ai-training-50000-fintech-lexpress) names artificial intelligence thirty-five times and funds a training platform, an investment tax credit and a forensic laboratory; the [Finance Bill](2026-07-27-lexpress-finance-bill-etat-pilote-par-les-donnees) itself is not held.
developments:
The budget carries a 50,000-trainee target, a Rs 25m national learning platform, an investment tax credit of 15 per cent a year over three years, a special economic zone of 83 arpents with preferential data-centre power and thirty-year renewable leases, electronic gates, an electronic visa, an electronic judiciary and a Rs 13m cyber forensic laboratory ([budget](2026-06-20-budget-2026-2027-ai-training-50000-fintech-lexpress)).

The accompanying 128-page Finance Bill is not held: three fetch paths into the assembly's bills library returned an HTML shell rather than the document, so the enacted tax and revenue measures cannot be read against the announcements ([bill](2026-07-27-lexpress-finance-bill-etat-pilote-par-les-donnees)).

summary: The [India relationship deepened](2026-04-09-mauritius-india-deepen-strategic-partnership) with new agreements in April 2026 and a tax treaty ratification approved in July.
developments:
New agreements were signed with India in April 2026 ([agreements](2026-04-09-mauritius-india-deepen-strategic-partnership)), and Cabinet approved ratification of the double taxation avoidance agreement in July ([Cabinet](2026-07-17-cabinet-highlights-dtaa-india-ratification)).

Domestically, the financial-sector agencies re-signed an amended memorandum of cooperation in March 2026 to strengthen coordination ([memorandum](2026-03-20-bom-amended-memorandum-of-cooperation-icc)).

The digital content of the India agreements is not itemised in the account held; what is dated is the relationship, not a named digital activity under it.

summary: The state operator's [2026-2029 strategy](2026-01-21-mauritius-telecom-strategy-2026-2029-bridging-africa-asia-lexpress) is a reported Rs 20bn programme across four corridors, and one [payments gateway](2026-05-18 Mauritius emerges as an African payments hub) reports volume growth above 300 per cent.
developments:
The four-corridor strategy covers connectivity, financial services, artificial intelligence and compute, and innovation, at a reported Rs 20bn; no delivery milestone has been published against it ([strategy](2026-01-21-mauritius-telecom-strategy-2026-2029-bridging-africa-asia-lexpress), [launch](2025-12-08-mauritius-telecom-connect-strategy-launch-techafricanews)).

One cross-border payments gateway reports its Mauritian entity grew transaction volume by over 300 per cent year on year and merchants by 42 per cent, serving over 150 companies, crediting exit from an international financial watchlist for the confidence ([gateway](2026-05-18 Mauritius emerges as an African payments hub)); the figures are the company's own ([gateway](2026-05-18 Mauritius emerges as an African payments hub)).

summary: A [development agency annual report](2026-08-25-undp-mauritius-annual-report-2025) for 2025 is held in full, and its digital component is not separately costed.
developments:
The report is a United Nations development agency's own account of its year in the country ([report](2026-08-25-undp-mauritius-annual-report-2025)).

The digital component is not separately costed in what is held, so the base can record that a partner is present and not what it spends on digital work. It is the only development-partner financing record in this unit.

summary: Mobile penetration is [reported in the 2025 ICT statistics](2026-07-10-ict-statistics-2025-internet-usage), a first observation on this ledger.
developments:
The statistics office's 2025 ICT release is the source of record ([release](2026-07-10-ict-statistics-2025-internet-usage)).

Two regulator decisions bear on what those subscriptions run over: the 700 MHz band opened in December 2025 ([decision](2025-12-22-icta-700mhz-imt-5g-decision)), and 3G is being phased out ([communique](2026-05-28-icta-phasing-out-3g-mobile-services)).

This is a first figure with no earlier observation held, so the level is stated and the direction is withheld. The 3G sunset has no switch-off date or migration figure behind it.

summary: Internet usage is [reported annually](2026-07-10-ict-statistics-2025-internet-usage) alongside household penetration indicators, with no earlier figure held here.
developments:
The 2025 ICT statistics carry usage and household penetration together ([release](2026-07-10-ict-statistics-2025-internet-usage)), on the household indicator series the promotion agency publishes ([indicators](2024-01-01-ict-households-digital-literacy-rate)).

Spectrum for mobile broadband was released in June 2026 ([decision](2026-06-04-icta-2300-2400mhz-imt-5g-decision)).

A first observation with no earlier one on this ledger. What the base does not hold is a rural-urban split, a gender split, or usage by income.

summary: A [free monthly mobile data package](2026-06-01-free-monthly-mobile-data-package-youth) for young people was added in June 2026 to the regulator's promotional tariff framework.
developments:
The regulator issued a promotional tariff framework in August 2025 ([directive](2025-08-18-icta-telecommunication-directive-3-of-2025)).

A free monthly mobile data package for young people is administered through the revenue authority ([package](2026-06-01-free-monthly-mobile-data-package-youth)).

Usage and penetration are reported annually ([statistics](2026-07-10-ict-statistics-2025-internet-usage)). Both instruments are interventions rather than measures: no price index, basket cost or affordability figure is held, so whether tariffs have moved cannot be read from the base.

summary: The backbone is in service under the [2030 strategic plan's](2018-12-17-digital-mauritius-2030-strategic-plan) connectivity pillar; no route length or capacity figure is held.
developments:
The 2030 strategic plan is the instrument the backbone sits under ([plan](2018-12-17-digital-mauritius-2030-strategic-plan)).

The incumbent used its December 2025 summit to position the island as the natural connector between Africa and Asia ([summit](2025-12-05-mt-connect-summit-agenda)).

What the base does not hold on this indicator is any physical figure — kilometres laid, lit capacity, or the number of exchanges reached. The connector claim rests on landings and geography rather than on a published domestic network.

summary: [Two ageing cables carry most international traffic](2026-08-02-google-amazon-et-maurice-les-coulisses-dun-tournant-numerique-majeur); a [new cable participation](2026-08-02-google-amazon-et-maurice-les-coulisses-dun-tournant-numerique-majeur) rests on a non-disclosure agreement, and [two further landings](2026-01-21-mauritius-telecom-strategy-2026-2029-bridging-africa-asia-lexpress) are named in an operator strategy.
developments:
Landings exist on four systems, two of which carry most international traffic, and the stated driver for new capacity is infrastructure ageing, with one cable due to retire around 2027 ([cables](2026-08-02-google-amazon-et-maurice-les-coulisses-dun-tournant-numerique-majeur), [estate](2025-07-16-hyperscale-data-hub-data-centres-telecomreviewafrica)).

The prime-ministerial commitment to join a new transoceanic cable sits behind a signed non-disclosure agreement and unfinished technical, legal and financial negotiation; no consortium confirmation, landing point, capacity, cost or service date is published, and the operator's own chief executive stayed non-specific on subsea at the same event ([commitment](2026-08-02-google-amazon-et-maurice-les-coulisses-dun-tournant-numerique-majeur), [summit](2026-07-16-mauritius-america-india-connect-subsea-cable-allmyt-summit-mitci), [report](2026-07-16-mauritius-joins-america-india-connect-cable)).

Two further landings are named as planned in the operator's strategy, one of them to replace the retiring cable, with no contract, cost or date published ([landings](2026-01-21-mauritius-telecom-strategy-2026-2029-bridging-africa-asia-lexpress)).

summary: The [exchange launched in 2015](2015-08-26-au-launches-internet-exchange-point-mauritius) runs public route servers on both address families; its size is known only from a third-party tracker.
developments:
It was launched in August 2015 with African Union support, to keep intra-country traffic in country ([launch](2015-08-26-au-launches-internet-exchange-point-mauritius)).

Its route servers and looking glass are publicly reachable on both address families ([looking glass](2026-06-15-mixp-route-server-looking-glass)).

The only account of its size is an external tracker's snapshot ([tracker](2026-05-01-ixp-tracker-mixp-snapshot)). The exchange publishes its infrastructure and not its traffic: no peer count, throughput figure or domestic-traffic share comes from the exchange itself.

summary: The [satellite authorisation regime](2025-05-22-mauritius-icta-ngso-satellite-decision) requires a locally licensed provider, a local point of presence and provider-retained terminals, and no service has been authorised under it.
developments:
Raphael Island in the Saint Brandon archipelago was connected to the internet ([report](2026-08-30-lexpress-saint-brandon-lile-raphael-se-connecte-a-internet)).

The regulator's decision of May 2025 permits service only through a locally licensed provider, with a local point of presence carrying Mauritian-geolocated addresses, real-time terminal dashboards and provider-retained terminal ownership ([decision](2025-05-22-mauritius-icta-ngso-satellite-decision)).

No satellite service has been authorised under it. Domestic experts are divided on its relevance given the country's existing fibre and mobile coverage ([debate](2026-07-02-mauritius-starlink-debate-defi-media)), which is the argument a small dense island makes against low-orbit service that larger neighbours cannot.

The ICT authority awarded a two-year contract on 28 August 2026 to provide satellite-based internet and communications to Raphael Island in the St Brandon archipelago, a first for the archipelago, intended to strengthen maritime monitoring, meteorological capability and safety in a cyclone-prone area ([contract](2026-08-28-platformafrica-emtel-icta-st-brandon-connectivity)). No service date, capacity or contract value is stated.

summary: [Ten facilities operate across five locations](2025-07-16-hyperscale-data-hub-data-centres-telecomreviewafrica), unchanged in count for a year, and a [carrier-neutral green data centre](2026-08-19-lexpress-mu-sadc-ramgoolam-carrier-neutral-green-centre) was announced at a regional summit in August 2026.
developments:
The estate is ten operating data centres across five towns, including a carrier-neutral facility designed to the highest resilience tier and the internet exchange point; no new facility has been reported since ([estate](2025-07-16-hyperscale-data-hub-data-centres-telecomreviewafrica)).

A carrier-neutral green data centre and a digital embassy village were announced at a regional summit in August 2026 as the digital leg of a bid to position the country as a regional hub, with no site, capacity, cost, operator or date stated ([announcement](2026-08-19-lexpress-mu-sadc-ramgoolam-carrier-neutral-green-centre)).

summary: The [Rose-Belle facility](2025-12-31-rose-belle-tier-iv-data-centre-national-strategy-lexpress) was certified to the highest resilience tier in December 2025 and hosts the government portal, the identity wallet and government artificial-intelligence workloads.
developments:
It hosts electronic health, the government portal, the mobile identity wallet, the penalty-points licence system and government artificial-intelligence workloads, giving the ageing government online centre the disaster recovery it lacked ([facility](2025-12-31-rose-belle-tier-iv-data-centre-national-strategy-lexpress)).

It is the country's sovereign-hosting anchor and the base holds no capacity, utilisation or tenant figure for it.

summary: A [central backup service](2026-09-01-cisd-computer-support-central-backup-service) runs for government, and a disaster recovery site is inside the current server and storage procurement.
developments:
The central information systems division operates a central backup service for government ([service](2026-09-01-cisd-computer-support-central-backup-service)).

High-performance servers, a storage area network and a backup solution for the main site and the disaster recovery site reached bid evaluation ([evaluation](2026-01-01-goc-san-executive-summary-bid-evaluation)), and a scale-out storage solution was awarded in March 2026 ([award](2026-03-27-goc-scale-out-storage-solution-award)).

The service page publishes no capacity, retention period or restoration-test record, and nothing states whether the disaster recovery site is in service.

summary: The [2026-2027 budget](2026-06-20-budget-2026-2027-ai-training-50000-fintech-lexpress) provides a special economic zone of 83 arpents with preferential data-centre power and thirty-year renewable leases.
developments:
The zone is the country's only stated arrangement connecting energy supply to data-centre siting ([budget](2026-06-20-budget-2026-2027-ai-training-50000-fintech-lexpress)).

No generation commitment, tariff, water assessment or outage measure for any facility is published, so the incentive is on record and the supply behind it is not.

summary: A [severe yellow alert followed a record 540 MW peak](2026-03-26-newsmoris-ceb-severe-yellow-alert) in March 2026, five months after a red alert.
developments:
The ministry's annual report for 2023-2024 is the standing account of network performance ([report](2024-11-05-mepu-annual-report-2023-2024)).

Business was urged to cut consumption under a red alert in October 2025 ([alert](2025-10-15-business-mauritius-ceb-red-alert)).

A severe yellow alert was triggered in March 2026 after electricity demand reached a record 540 MW peak ([alert](2026-03-26-newsmoris-ceb-severe-yellow-alert)). The alert colours are the utility's own scale; no reserve margin, outage duration or loss figure is published against them.

summary: Electrification is universal on the main island; the live decisions are [a household solar scheme](2026-04-11-ceb-solar-photovoltaic-scheme-households-2026) and outer-island extensions.
developments:
The ministry reports annually on network performance ([report](2024-11-05-mepu-annual-report-2023-2024)).

The Rodrigues executive council took electricity extension decisions in February 2026 ([decisions](2026-02-06-rra-executive-council-decisions-electricity-extension)).

A household solar photovoltaic scheme opened for 2026 ([scheme](2026-04-11-ceb-solar-photovoltaic-scheme-households-2026)). The indicator reads differently here than on the continent: connection is not the open question, and what the base tracks instead is generation at the household and on the outer islands.

summary: Government servers, storage and a disaster recovery site are [in procurement](2026-01-01-goc-san-executive-summary-bid-evaluation), alongside a sovereign cloud market sounding.
developments:
The 2025-2029 blueprint sets the modernisation of government platforms as a workstream ([blueprint](2025-05-27-blueprint-for-mauritius-digital-transformation-2025-2029)).

High-performance servers, a storage area network and a backup solution for the main and disaster recovery sites reached bid evaluation ([evaluation](2026-01-01-goc-san-executive-summary-bid-evaluation)).

A sovereign cloud for government is being market-sounded in parallel ([clarification](2025-09-19-sovereign-cloud-rfi-clarification-no-2)). No availability figure, incident record or capacity statement for the existing estate is held, so the case for replacement rests on procurement documents rather than on published performance.

summary: An [information security management system](2026-03-10-isms-half-day-workshop-public-service) is being advanced across the public service from March 2026.
developments:
The digital government transformation strategy reported progress for the first time on file in April 2025 ([update](2025-04-25-digital-government-transformation-strategy-progress-update)).

A half-day workshop programme is advancing an information security management system across the public service ([workshop](2026-03-10-isms-half-day-workshop-public-service)).

No certification, scope statement or completion date accompanies it, and no establishment figure, vacancy rate or retention account for specialist digital posts is held anywhere in the base.

summary: A [critical information infrastructure regime](2026-05-22-cybersecurity-critical-infrastructure-regulations-2026-lexpress) came into force in June 2026 across six sectors, a [threat-sharing platform](2026-07-24-mauritius-economic-financial-measures-misc-provisions-bill-xiii-2026) is provided for, and a [forensic laboratory](2026-06-20-budget-2026-2027-ai-training-50000-fintech-lexpress) is funded.
developments:
The designation regulations are in force across financial and banking, public service, information technology and broadcasting, energy and water, and transport, with a twelve-month compliance window and non-compliance carrying up to twenty-five years' imprisonment and fines up to Rs 2m ([regime](2026-05-22-cybersecurity-critical-infrastructure-regulations-2026-lexpress), [framework](2026-06-30-cii-cyber-laws-framework-itweb)).

The omnibus bill would empower the central bank to establish a cyber threat intelligence sharing platform and to require financial institutions, and other institutions it specifies, to participate on terms it determines; participation is compulsory and the perimeter is set by the central bank rather than by the cyber authority ([platform](2026-07-24-mauritius-economic-financial-measures-misc-provisions-bill-xiii-2026)).

A cyber forensic laboratory is funded at Rs 13m alongside an information-security management system across the administration, with no site, staffing or opening date published ([laboratory](2026-06-20-budget-2026-2027-ai-training-50000-fintech-lexpress)), against more than 4,000 reported cyber incidents since January 2026 ([incidents](2026-08-14-mauritius-telecom-cybersecurity-ai-schools-programme)).

summary: The Finance Bill would empower the [statistics office to share more data with the finance ministry](2026-07-27-lexpress-finance-bill-etat-pilote-par-les-donnees), alongside new declaration duties on public bodies.
developments:
The provision was before Parliament in July 2026 and its enacting text is not held ([provision](2026-07-27-lexpress-finance-bill-etat-pilote-par-les-donnees)).

The expanded inter-agency sharing arrives with no matching amendment to the data protection statute, and the interoperability framework it would run over dates from 2002. Those two facts together are the exchange position of this unit.

summary: The [government superapp soft-launched](2026-01-30-korek-super-app-soft-launch) in January 2026 on verifiable credentials in a secure identity wallet.
developments:
A request for information was issued in September 2025 for a superapp built on verifiable digital credentials in a secure identity wallet ([request](2025-09-11-superapp-verifiable-credentials-rfi)).

It soft-launched as KOREK! in January 2026 ([launch](2026-01-30-korek-super-app-soft-launch)).

The mobile identity wallet it draws on has been in service since February 2025. What the base does not hold is a list of the services the credential now opens, or a transaction count through any of them.

summary: The e-Health programme [targets full public-sector coverage by end-2027](2026-07-12-secteur-public-e-health-couverture-complete-2027), thirteen years after it started.
developments:
The ministry reported on its performance for 2024-2025 ([report](2025-10-30-mohw-annual-report-performance-fy2024-2025)).

An account of July 2026 puts full public-sector coverage at the end of 2027, thirteen years into the programme ([account](2026-07-12-secteur-public-e-health-couverture-complete-2027)).

A modernised public health bill was put to a stakeholder workshop in May 2026 ([workshop](2026-05-22-public-health-bill-2026-workshop)). The 2027 target is the programme's own, and no coverage figure against it is published.

summary: A [data infrastructure was tendered](2026-02-20-hec-data-lake-consultancy-notice) for the higher education regulator in February 2026, under a 2025-2035 sector strategy.
developments:
The national strategy for higher education, science and research covers 2025 to 2035 ([strategy](2025-01-01-national-strategy-higher-education-science-research-2025-2035)).

Consultancy services for a comprehensive and robust data infrastructure were put out to bid for the higher education regulator ([notice](2026-02-20-hec-data-lake-consultancy-notice)).

An education platform pilot was agreed with the incumbent operator in October 2025 ([agreement](2025-10-28-mytgpt-educational-platform-pilot-mou)). Nothing in the base records an exchange between the education systems and the identity or civil registration layers.

summary: An [e-Social Security system was tendered](2025-10-22-e-social-security-system-tender) in October 2025 over a social register decided in Cabinet in 2009.
developments:
The social register was decided in Cabinet in March 2009 ([decision](2009-03-26-cabinet-decisions-social-register-mauritius)).

An e-Social Security system was put out to tender in October 2025 for supply, installation, testing, commissioning and maintenance ([tender](2025-10-22-e-social-security-system-tender)).

Cabinet used the register in February 2026 to target a free-internet measure ([Cabinet](2026-02-06-cabinet-highlights-internet-gratis-srm)) — the clearest evidence held that the register is joined to another system's delivery, and the only such use on file.

summary: The [national authentication framework was put to an independent security audit](2025-10-13-mitci-maupass-security-audit-ifb-press-notice) tendered in October 2025.
developments:
The identity card regulations of February 2024 set the terms on which the card and the mobile identity are issued and read ([regulations](2024-02-16-national-identity-card-regulations-2024)).

A consultancy firm was sought in October 2025 for an independent information-technology security audit of the national authentication framework ([notice](2025-10-13-mitci-maupass-security-audit-ifb-press-notice)).

The servers the framework runs on are inside a separate procurement, alongside a sovereign cloud market sounding ([clarification](2025-09-19-sovereign-cloud-rfi-clarification-no-2)). The audit was commissioned; no finding, availability figure or incident record from it is held.

summary: Registration runs under the [1981 Civil Status Act](1982-01-01-civil-status-act-version-7-cpd-csd), with a further [issuing centre tendered](2025-12-15-curepipe-registration-issuance-centre-tender) in December 2025.
developments:
The Act has been in force since January 1982 and is held in its consolidated form ([Act](1982-01-01-civil-status-act-version-7-cpd-csd)).

Office space was put out to open national bidding in December 2025 for a further registration and issuance centre of the identity card unit ([tender](2025-12-15-curepipe-registration-issuance-centre-tender)).

The Finance Act 2026 amends the statute book around the registers ([Act](2026-08-12-finance-act-2026)). No coverage rate, enrolment count or backlog figure for the population register is published in the sources held.

summary: The omnibus bill would make [permits issuable in digital, card or paper form](2026-07-24-mauritius-economic-financial-measures-misc-provisions-bill-xiii-2026) and impose a digital travel authorisation on visa-exempt arrivals.
developments:
The authorisation would be applied for electronically and paid before travel; the bill was introduced and not enacted ([provision](2026-07-24-mauritius-economic-financial-measures-misc-provisions-bill-xiii-2026)).

It is the first credential in the base whose form is set by statute rather than by the issuing agency, which is what makes the digital form enforceable rather than optional.

summary: The [Mobile ID wallet](2024-09-06 Mauritius Launches Mobile ID Digital Wallet with Thales - First African ISO-standard Digital ID Wallet) has been in service since September 2024 and is hosted on the sovereign facility, with no user or issuance figure published.
developments:
The wallet launched in September 2024 with a foreign vendor under the 2024 national identity card regulations ([launch](2024-09-06 Mauritius Launches Mobile ID Digital Wallet with Thales - First African ISO-standard Digital ID Wallet), [regulations](2024-01-01 National Identity Card (Mobile ID) Regulations 2024 (Mauritius))).

It is now hosted on the Rose-Belle facility and still carries no published user or issuance figure. A domestic analysis welcomed its convenience and pressed for privacy and surveillance safeguards around the enabling regulations ([analysis](2025-02-06 Smart and Mobile ID in Mauritius - Recommendations for a Balanced Approach)).

summary: The [1985 identity card Act](1986-04-11-national-identity-card-act-version-3) governs issue, and the base holds no provision assigning an identifier at birth.
developments:
The Act has been in force since April 1986 ([Act](1986-04-11-national-identity-card-act-version-3)).

Statistical and registry measures were carried in the 2026-2027 budget annex ([annex](2026-06-19-budget-annex-2026-27-statistics-act-independence)).

What the base does not hold is any provision assigning a unique identifier at birth, any linkage rule between the birth register and the card, or a figure for how many newborns are registered. The card is an adult instrument on the record as it stands.

summary: The [verifiable-credential wallet](2025-10-02-superapp-digital-wallet-clarification-no-1) is the route by which civil-status records could reach the identity layer; nothing yet flows.
developments:
Birth registration runs under the Civil Status Act in its 2023-revised form ([Act](1982-01-01-civil-status-act-2023-revision-birth-registration)).

A clarification of October 2025 set the shape of the secure identity wallet the superapp is built on ([clarification](2025-10-02-superapp-digital-wallet-clarification-no-1)).

Registry and identity systems are carried together in the public sector investment programme for 2026-2027 to 2030-2031 ([programme](2026-06-19-psip-2026-2027-to-2030-2031)). No integration between birth registration and the identity system is recorded as operating.

summary: [SIM registration by electronic identity check](2024-01-01 eKYC Steps for Mauritian Citizen (SIM Re-Registration)) has been in use since the re-registration exercise, with no completion or coverage figure held.
developments:
The electronic verification steps were published for the re-registration exercise and remain in use ([steps](2024-01-01 eKYC Steps for Mauritian Citizen (SIM Re-Registration))).

No completion or coverage figure is held, and no other system is recorded taking the national identity as its authentication, so the identity layer's reach into other sectors cannot be established from this base.

summary: A [National Fintech Strategy 2026-2030](2026-06-29-national-fintech-strategy-2026-2030-wearetech) was presented in June 2026, a [governance committee](2026-07-24-mauritius-economic-financial-measures-misc-provisions-bill-xiii-2026) put on a statutory footing, and a [digital onboarding system](2026-02-04-bom-digital-payments-workshop-lexpress) is under construction.
developments:
The strategy runs six pillars carrying a governance committee, open banking, an artificial-intelligence push in finance and a business facilitation bill, implemented with the central bank ([strategy](2026-06-29-national-fintech-strategy-2026-2030-wearetech)).

The committee is provided for in a new part of the financial services statute from September 2026, minister-chaired, seating the central bank governor, the financial regulator's chief executive, two ministries, the investment board and four private-sector members, empowered to approve sector-wide standards and expressly not a body corporate ([committee](2026-07-24-mauritius-economic-financial-measures-misc-provisions-bill-xiii-2026), [account](2026-06-29-national-fintech-strategy-2026-2030-wearetech)).

A know-your-customer system for digital onboarding is under construction alongside alignment to an international cross-border roadmap and exploratory work on fraud detection, with no delivery date published ([onboarding](2026-02-04-bom-digital-payments-workshop-lexpress)).

progress: No change, a standing allowance with no earlier position held
summary: A [social contribution income allowance](2026-01-01-csg-income-allowance-faq) is administered by the revenue authority, with eligibility and payment terms published.
developments:
The revenue authority publishes the allowance's terms in a frequently-asked-questions document of January 2026 ([document](2026-01-01-csg-income-allowance-faq)).

The 2026-2030 fintech strategy sets out the payment rails such transfers run over ([strategy](2026-05-22-mauritius-national-fintech-strategy-2026-2030)).

No payment volume, disbursement channel breakdown or coverage rate is published for the allowance, so the base can say the mechanism exists and not how much of the population it reaches or by what route.

summary: Value-added tax on [digital services from foreign suppliers](2026-01-01-mra-vat-digital-services-foreign-suppliers) is being collected, with a supplier guide now at version 2.0.
developments:
The central bank's annual report for the year to June 2024 is the standing account of the payment system revenue runs over ([report](2024-10-30-bank-of-mauritius-annual-report-2023-24)).

The revenue authority collects value-added tax on digital and electronic services supplied from abroad ([regime](2026-01-01-mra-vat-digital-services-foreign-suppliers)), and its guide for foreign suppliers is at version 2.0 ([guide](2026-01-01-mra-guide-foreign-suppliers-digital-services)).

No collection figure under the regime is published, and no count of registered foreign suppliers is held.

summary: The [central switch](2019-08-14-maucas-bank-of-mauritius-page) routes payments around the clock, and payment aggregators were brought under guideline in July 2026.
developments:
The central automated switch is owned and operated by the central bank and routes payments among operators on a 24-hour basis ([switch](2019-08-14-maucas-bank-of-mauritius-page)).

A guideline for payment aggregators was issued in July 2026, bringing them under a stated supervisory expectation for the first time ([guideline](2026-07-01-guideline-for-payment-aggregators)).

Business-to-business measures were carried in the 2026-2027 budget ([budget](2026-06-19-budget-speech-2026-2027-startup-revolution)). No transaction volume through the switch is published in the sources held.

summary: The [instant payment switch](2024-01-01 SIIPS 2024 Case Study - MauCAS (Mauritius)) is a mature interoperable rail with a code standard, and the largest bank reports [code payments up 67 per cent](2026-01-19-mcb-qr-payments-67pc-growth-lexpress) with cash down to 27 per cent of consumer spend.
developments:
The switch was profiled as a mature interoperable national rail with a code standard in a 2024 instant-payments review, and no national transaction volume has been published since ([switch](2024-01-01 SIIPS 2024 Case Study - MauCAS (Mauritius))).

The largest bank's 2025 figures put cash at 27 per cent of consumer spend against 30 per cent a year earlier, code payments up 67 per cent year on year, contactless above six in ten card transactions and about 18,000 merchants accepting ([adoption](2026-01-19-mcb-qr-payments-67pc-growth-lexpress)); they are one bank's figures rather than a national series ([adoption](2026-01-19-mcb-qr-payments-67pc-growth-lexpress)).

progress: No change, a first published user count with nothing earlier behind it
summary: The state operator's wallet reports [over 130,000 active users](2026-01-21-mauritius-telecom-strategy-2026-2029-bridging-africa-asia-lexpress), being built into a cross-border product, with no transaction figure published.
developments:
The figure comes from the operator's 2026-2029 strategy ([wallet](2026-01-21-mauritius-telecom-strategy-2026-2029-bridging-africa-asia-lexpress)).

No earlier user count is held, so the level is recorded and the direction is not. It is the only wallet uptake figure in the base for a country whose broadband penetration is above saturation, which makes the wallet the laggard rather than the network.

summary: An [India payment link](2026-02-04-bom-digital-payments-workshop-lexpress) has run since 2024, a [Seychelles corridor](2026-07-16-mauritius-telecom-allmyt-keynote-sovereign-ai-platformafrica) was announced in July 2026, and the rupee is [reported as considered](2026-07-29-sadc-rtgs-currencies-centralbanking) for regional settlement.
developments:
The bilateral cross-border payments link with India was the country's first, in force since February 2024, with no volume or corridor figure published ([link](2026-02-04-bom-digital-payments-workshop-lexpress)).

A corridor with Seychelles was announced as launched by the state operator at its summit, with no corroborating record from the partner, the central bank or the counterpart central bank on file ([corridor](2026-07-16-mauritius-telecom-allmyt-keynote-sovereign-ai-platformafrica)).

Onboarding the rupee to the regional settlement system is reported as under consideration, potentially by the end of 2027, on a spokesperson's account from another central bank; no domestic statement is held, and the named next currencies are two others ([settlement](2026-07-29-sadc-rtgs-currencies-centralbanking)).

summary: The [2018 payment systems Act](2019-01-31-national-payment-systems-act-2018) is the statutory base, and [stablecoin guidance](2026-08-13-fsc-guidance-notes-stablecoins) was issued in August 2026.
developments:
The Act is at its seventh consolidated version and is the statute under which payment providers are licensed and supervised ([Act](2019-01-31-national-payment-systems-act-2018)).

The financial services regulator issued guidance notes on stablecoins with an annexure in August 2026, as part of its fintech series ([guidance](2026-08-13-fsc-guidance-notes-stablecoins)).

Neither instrument is a consumer redress mechanism. No complaint volume, resolution rate or compensation arrangement for payment users is held anywhere in the base.

summary: The civil status register's [system is being replaced](2025-09-02-csd-system-revamping-communique-registry), announced September 2025, with the 2026 Finance Act amending around it.
developments:
The register operates under the Civil Status Act of 1981 ([Act](1982-01-01-civil-status-act-version-7-cpd-csd)).

The civil status division announced a revamping of its system in September 2025 ([communique](2025-09-02-csd-system-revamping-communique-registry)).

The Finance Act 2026 carries the statutory changes behind the budget's registry measures ([Act](2026-08-12-finance-act-2026)). No completeness figure, record count or migration timetable for the replacement is published.

summary: The [civil registration base](2024-01-01 Mauritius Civil Status Division Annual Report on Performance FY2023-2024) is recorded as complete and underpinning the identity system, on a performance report for 2023-2024.
developments:
The civil status division's performance report for 2023-2024 is the most recent account held ([report](2024-01-01 Mauritius Civil Status Division Annual Report on Performance FY2023-2024), [presentation](2019-06-01 The CRVS and Identity Eco-System in the Republic of Mauritius (presentation))).

No later performance report is held, and no registration rate, backlog or error measure has been published since. A complete base is the assumption on which the identity wallet and the social-security digitisation both rest.

progress: No change, a searched absence the data strategy itself names
summary: No national address register exists; the [national data strategy](2026-01-28-mauritius-national-data-strategy) identifies addressing as a data gap.
developments:
The strategy of January 2026 is the instrument that names the gap ([strategy](2026-01-28-mauritius-national-data-strategy)).

The closest work on file is the verifiable-credential wallet's identity attributes, market-sounded in September 2025 ([request](2025-09-11-superapp-verifiable-credentials-rfi)).

The island's postal addressing is not organised as a state register, and no addressing standard, register or mandate for one is held. The absence is dated and searched rather than unexamined.

summary: The register runs under the [2006 Act](2006-10-01-business-registration-act) and feeds [quarterly enterprise statistics](2026-07-29-business-statistics-q2-2026).
developments:
The Business Registration Act has been in force since October 2006 ([Act](2006-10-01-business-registration-act)).

The register feeds quarterly enterprise-dynamics statistics, published for the second quarter of 2026 in July ([statistics](2026-07-29-business-statistics-q2-2026)).

The economic and financial measures bill debated in July 2026 touches its statutory base ([debate](2026-07-31-parliamentary-debate-economic-financial-measures-bill)). No registration volume, processing time or online-share figure for the register itself is held.

summary: The [social register](2009-03-26-cabinet-decisions-social-register-mauritius) targeted the 2026-2027 budget's measures and a free-internet decision, with its platform being replaced.
developments:
The register was decided in Cabinet in March 2009 ([decision](2009-03-26-cabinet-decisions-social-register-mauritius)).

Cabinet used it in February 2026 to target a free-internet measure ([Cabinet](2026-02-06-cabinet-highlights-internet-gratis-srm)), and the 2026-2027 budget's measures are targeted on it ([budget](2026-06-19-budget-speech-2026-2027-startup-revolution)).

The social integration division reported on its performance for 2024-2025 ([report](2026-07-01-social-integration-division-annual-report)). No enrolment figure for the register is published in any source held.

summary: The register is compiled annually from a [statutory house-to-house inquiry](2026-01-14-house-to-house-inquiry-2026); no digital enrolment route is described.
developments:
The Representation of the People Act requires a house-to-house inquiry for the compilation of the register, carried out again in 2026 ([inquiry](2026-01-14-house-to-house-inquiry-2026)).

The electoral commissioner issued a public communique on elector registration in May 2026 ([communique](2026-05-14-communique-enregistrement-electeurs-2026)).

The inquiry is a door-to-door canvass. In a country whose identity card carries a mobile form and whose government runs a credential wallet, the electoral roll is still compiled by knocking on doors.

summary: The register extended in two directions inside a year: a [changed VAT threshold](2025-09-12-mra-compulsory-vat-registration-communique) and a [tax agent registration regime](2026-06-30-mra-registration-of-tax-agents-guide).
developments:
The register is maintained under the Income Tax Act, in force since July 1996 ([Act](1996-07-01-income-tax-act)).

The compulsory value-added tax registration threshold changed following the Finance Act, notified in September 2025 ([communique](2025-09-12-mra-compulsory-vat-registration-communique)).

A registration regime opened for tax agents, with eligibility, procedure and obligations published in June 2026 ([guide](2026-06-30-mra-registration-of-tax-agents-guide)). No registered-taxpayer count is published in the sources held.

summary: A [disaster recovery solution](2026-03-20-rgd-disaster-recovery-mers-communique) was implemented for the electronic registry in March 2026, with deed e-submission in the budget annex.
developments:
The registry operates under a statute of 1864 ([Act](1864-06-01-transcription-and-mortgage-act)), and the department reported on its performance for 2024-2025 ([report](2025-10-01-rgd-annual-report-2024-2025)).

A disaster recovery solution was implemented for the electronic registry system in March 2026 ([communique](2026-03-20-rgd-disaster-recovery-mers-communique)).

Electronic submission of land deeds is carried in the 2026-2027 budget annex ([annex](2026-06-25-annex-budget-speech-2026-2027-land-deeds-e-submission)). The registry is digital and resilient; the statute beneath it is 162 years old.

summary: The [eHealth strategy](2015-01-01 Health 2015 - Seamless Continuity of Care (Mauritius eHealth strategy)) dates from 2015 and no successor or delivery report is held, though health workloads now run on the sovereign facility.
developments:
The continuity-of-care strategy published in 2015 is the standing instrument ([strategy](2015-01-01 Health 2015 - Seamless Continuity of Care (Mauritius eHealth strategy))).

Electronic health workloads are hosted on the Rose-Belle facility, so the hosting has moved and the strategy governing what is hosted has not. No successor strategy, delivery report, record count or facility coverage figure is held.

summary: The [education pilot](2026-01-26-mytgpt-education-pilot-techreviewafrica) on the sovereign artificial-intelligence platform was narrowed from a student tutor to a teacher assistant after teacher and parent resistance.
developments:
The pilot was deliberately narrowed on pedagogical rather than technical grounds to homework correction and exam generation, targeting one per secondary teacher by 2027 ([pilot](2026-01-26-mytgpt-education-pilot-techreviewafrica), [keynote](2026-07-16-mauritius-telecom-allmyt-keynote-sovereign-ai-platformafrica)).

The operator's chief executive put the platform's exam-marking tools at 99 per cent accuracy across the tools introduced ([interview](2026-08-16-mauritius-telecom-ceo-aws-partnership-interview)). It is a rare documented narrowing of an African education deployment, and the reason it narrowed is recorded ([argument](2026-07-13-gungadin-ai-economic-pillar-interview-mauritiustimes)).

summary: [10.5m social-benefit documents](2026-06-02-e-social-security-digitization-welfare-wearetech) are being digitised into a future platform, after thirteen years of the welfare system running on paper.
developments:
Bulk scanning of beneficiary files began in May 2026 with full integration stated at about eighteen months; the system carries about 800,000 payments a month to at least 350,000 beneficiaries ([digitisation](2026-06-02-e-social-security-digitization-welfare-wearetech)).

Social-protection spending was Rs 91.4bn, 12.8 per cent of gross domestic product, in 2024-25 ([spending](2026-06-02-e-social-security-digitization-welfare-wearetech)), which is the scale the paper system was carrying.

progress: No change, an investment line with nothing recorded as operating
summary: Court systems are [carried in the 2026-2031 investment programme](2026-06-19-psip-2026-2027-to-2030-2031) and in the e-judiciary component; nothing is recorded as operating.
developments:
Justice systems appear in the public sector investment programme for 2026-2027 to 2030-2031 ([programme](2026-06-19-psip-2026-2027-to-2030-2031)).

The government's own justice information page describes the aim rather than a system ([page](2026-09-01-govmu-justice-info-page)).

The e-judiciary sits in the same package as e-Gates and e-Visa, all planned. No case-management system, filing volume or rollout figure is held, so the base can record an intention and not a capability.

progress: No change, a phased rollout with no phase reported
summary: An [e-invoicing system](2023-06-26-mra-e-invoicing-system) is being introduced nationally in a phased approach; no phase schedule or volume is published.
developments:
The revenue authority is introducing an e-invoicing system at national level in a phase-wise approach ([system](2023-06-26-mra-e-invoicing-system)).

Value-added tax on digital services from foreign suppliers runs alongside it ([regime](2026-01-01-mra-vat-digital-services-foreign-suppliers)).

The page held carries no phase schedule, taxpayer count or invoice volume. Three years after the announcement, the base cannot say how far the rollout has reached.

summary: Customs hosted a [World Customs Organization cloud study mission](2026-01-20-wco-study-mission-cloud-computing-mauritius-customs) in January 2026, on regulations made in 1997.
developments:
Computerised customs declaration has a statutory basis in regulations of April 1997 ([regulations](1997-04-19-customs-use-of-computer-regulations)).

A study mission on cloud computing was hosted by the customs administration in January 2026 ([mission](2026-01-20-wco-study-mission-cloud-computing-mauritius-customs)).

The export procedure under China zero-tariff treatment was put onto the trade platform in May 2026 ([notice](2026-05-19-mra-notice-export-china-zero-tariff-tradenet)). The country is teaching cloud practice to its peers on a legal basis written before the platform existed.

summary: The land administration system is [being replaced](2026-03-27-lavims-2-0-consultant-selection-notice), with consultant selection opened in March 2026 for a second-generation solution.
developments:
The system's statutory basis is the Cadastral Survey Act 2011 ([Act](2011-07-15-cadastral-survey-act-2011)).

A consultant selection was opened in March 2026 for a turnkey second-generation solution ([notice](2026-03-27-lavims-2-0-consultant-selection-notice)).

The deeds registry beside it took a disaster recovery solution in the same month ([communique](2026-03-20-rgd-disaster-recovery-mers-communique)). No parcel count, coverage figure or transaction volume for the current system is held, so what the replacement improves on is not on the record.

summary: An [online motor vehicle licence and road tax service](2026-08-18-mauritius-online-licensing-road-tax-taxis) launched in August 2026, with [electronic gates, visa and judiciary](2026-06-20-budget-2026-2027-ai-training-50000-fintech-lexpress) funded and a [clinical-trial licensing system](2026-07-24-mauritius-economic-financial-measures-misc-provisions-bill-xiii-2026) provided for in statute.
developments:
The licence and road tax service is live for taxi operators, who renew and pay online instead of at post offices and counters, and the ministry states it will also build a database of operators; the transport authority's underlying system is stated as outdated with a tender launched to upgrade it ([service](2026-08-18-mauritius-online-licensing-road-tax-taxis)).

Electronic gates, an electronic visa and an electronic judiciary are funded in the budget alongside a healthcare innovation and artificial-intelligence unit, with no procurement, vendor or delivery date published ([funding](2026-06-20-budget-2026-2027-ai-training-50000-fintech-lexpress)).

The omnibus bill would put concurrent submission, review and processing of clinical-trial applications through a statutory electronic system, with the council and ethics committee empowered to meet virtually; the electronic channel and the procedure that runs on it are in the same statute, which makes the channel enforceable against the regulator ([licensing](2026-07-24-mauritius-economic-financial-measures-misc-provisions-bill-xiii-2026)). A metrology platform for bookings, payments and certificates is separately in build ([metrology](2026-08-10-mauritius-legal-metrology-digitization)).

summary: Local authorities were [given more autonomous and digital management](2026-02-20-vers-une-gestion-autonome-digitale-collectivites-locales) in February 2026; no platform is named.
developments:
The ministry reports annually on local government performance ([2023-2024](2024-01-01-annual-report-local-government-2023-2024-records), [2024-2025](2025-01-01-annual-report-local-government-2024-2025)).

A decisive step towards more autonomous and digital management of local authorities was taken in February 2026 ([step](2026-02-20-vers-une-gestion-autonome-digitale-collectivites-locales)).

Government servers and storage are being procured centrally ([evaluation](2026-01-01-goc-san-executive-summary-bid-evaluation)). What the base does not hold is any account of what local authorities themselves run: no equipment programme, connectivity figure or platform is named.

summary: Local government records appear only in [ministry annual reports](2024-01-01-annual-report-local-government-2023-2024-records); the February 2026 step is the first digital commitment held.
developments:
Records are described in the ministry's annual performance reports for 2023-2024 and 2024-2025 ([2023-2024](2024-01-01-annual-report-local-government-2023-2024-records), [2024-2025](2025-01-01-annual-report-local-government-2024-2025)).

The February 2026 decision on autonomous and digital management of local authorities is the first dated commitment on file ([decision](2026-02-20-vers-une-gestion-autonome-digitale-collectivites-locales)).

No digitisation programme, record count or system is named for local authority records. The national registries are being replaced one by one; the municipal layer has no equivalent on the record.

summary: [Electrical works were awarded](2026-05-21-award-electrical-works-ehealth-region2-ahc-chc) in May 2026 for e-Health in the second region's area and community health centres.
developments:
Electrical works for area and community health centres in the second e-Health region were awarded in May 2026 ([award](2026-05-21-award-electrical-works-ehealth-region2-ahc-chc)).

Full public-sector coverage is targeted for the end of 2027, thirteen years into the programme ([account](2026-07-12-secteur-public-e-health-couverture-complete-2027)).

The ministry's own performance report for 2024-2025 is the standing account ([report](2025-10-30-mohw-annual-report-performance-fy2024-2025)). No count of centres connected against the target is published.

summary: Two programmes run in primary schools: [virtual reality](2026-09-01-virtual-reality-primary-schools-vrps) and an education platform launched in January 2026.
developments:
A virtual reality programme runs in primary schools ([programme](2026-09-01-virtual-reality-primary-schools-vrps)).

An education platform was launched in January 2026 under a pilot agreed with the incumbent operator ([launch](2026-01-31-lancement-transformation-numerique-mytgpt-education)).

Household ICT penetration is reported annually ([statistics](2026-07-10-ict-statistics-2025-internet-usage)). Neither programme publishes a school count or a pupil reach, and no school connectivity figure is held.

summary: The civil status division's [system is being replaced](2025-09-02-csd-system-revamping-communique-registry) and the deeds registry reports annually; there is no separate rural network.
developments:
The deeds registry reported on its performance for 2024-2025 ([report](2025-10-01-rgd-annual-report-2024-2025)).

The civil status division announced a system revamping in September 2025 ([communique](2025-09-02-csd-system-revamping-communique-registry)).

The indicator reads differently on an island of this size: there is no rural registry network in the sense it asks about, and the offices are a small national estate reached by the same replacement programmes as everything else.

summary: Digitisation is carried in the force's [strategic plan for 2026 to 2028](2025-12-31-mpf-strategic-plan-2026-2028), published December 2025.
developments:
The force reported on its performance for 2024-2025 ([report](2025-10-01-mpf-annual-report-2024-2025)).
